---
title: "From a panel to its analysis"
subtitle: "Three levels of reproducibility, with explicit starting points."
---

## 01 · Read the evidence

The five chapters present saved analytical results alongside their methods and
source code. Reading does not require R, Python or access to the original server.
The current website is a **documentation build**, not a fresh statistical run.

## 02 · Recreate a panel from checkpoints

The executable R Markdown documents and chapter scripts live in `analyses/`.
They expect processed inputs at chapter-relative paths. Code stays in GitHub;
numerical inputs are supplied separately as five figure-specific ZIP archives
in Zenodo data package v1. The [data catalogue](datasets.qmd) lists their exact
filenames and sizes.

**Status: UNPUBLISHED / RESTRICTED DRAFT.** The eight files have been uploaded
and the draft saved. DOI
[10.5281/zenodo.23266285](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23266285) is reserved and
**not active until publication**. Private reviewer access to the files is issued
separately from access to the GitHub code; no private preview link belongs in
this repository.

The package records compatible code commit
[`ada517267dce6d2665710d79f3d73b54f0cba50b`](https://github.com/BolisLab/mir29/commit/ada517267dce6d2665710d79f3d73b54f0cba50b).
Use that revision or a documented compatible successor. Check the
[manifest](https://github.com/BolisLab/mir29/blob/main/data/zenodo-manifest.json)
and [SHA-256 list](https://github.com/BolisLab/mir29/blob/main/data/zenodo-SHA256SUMS.txt),
then extract the desired ZIPs **into the repository root**. Each archive already
contains `analyses/FigureN_and_SN/`, so extraction restores the expected paths;
do not extract inside a figure's `data/` directory. Compare hashes before merging
with existing inputs. A missing file must be restored from its verified source,
not substituted with rounded values read from a figure.

| Chapter | Renderer, run from the corresponding chapter directory |
|:--|:--|
| Figure 1 + S1 | `Rscript render_figure1_and_s1.R` |
| Figure 2 + S2 | `Rscript render_figure2_and_s2.R` |
| Figure 3 + S3 | `Rscript render_figure3_and_s3.R` |
| Figure 4 + S4 | `Rscript render_figure4_and_s4.R` |
| Figure 5 + S5 | `Rscript render_figure5_and_s5.R` |

Restore the inputs, match the recorded software versions, then execute in the
chapter directory. The renderer may write regenerated figures and tables there.
Do not install a new package version merely to make an old analysis run without
checking whether it changes the result.

### Remaining execution limits

The archives support replay from processed checkpoints, but do not make every
unmodified notebook executable in a fresh environment:

- **Figure 1 + S1:** `data/epiclock_preds_GTEX.RDS` is intentionally withheld
  because it contains controlled GTEx donor-level information. The notebook reads
  it during initialization, so a full unmodified render requires authorised local
  data. The aggregate-input helper for S1a,b,f,g,h,i can run without that object.
- **Figure 4 + S4:** `data/primary/gtex_sample_metrics.rds` is intentionally
  withheld. The DNAm-age window module reads it even though aggregate windows
  are included. A full unmodified render requires the authorised local input
  or a separately documented code update.
- **Figure 3 + S3:** when `digest` is installed, the standard renderer automatically
  runs a post-render hash check requiring two original reference PDFs that are
  not included. Without them, this check fails even if HTML rendering has completed.
  Analysis inputs and PNG references do not replace these PDFs.

GTEx access must be obtained through the appropriate dbGaP permissions; the
Zenodo draft does not confer it. The Figure 5 reference-selection object alone
occupies about 1.6 GB when loaded in R, with additional memory needed for the
remaining objects and calculations. File-integrity and targeted numerical checks
are distinct from a clean-environment render of all five notebooks; no complete
raw-data rerun or such five-notebook render is claimed.

## 03 · Repeat upstream processing

Raw-read alignment, normalisation, genome-wide model fitting and predictor
training are separate from checkpoint-to-panel reconstruction. Their source
code and provenance are being consolidated. The documentation does **not**
claim that a single command currently reproduces the entire paper from raw data.

For small RNA, distinguish nf-core/smrnaseq reprocessing from analyses that used
published processed matrices. For methylation, distinguish IDAT preprocessing
and genome-wide discovery from the compact panel-level inputs. Controlled-access
metadata must be obtained through the appropriate access process.

## Statistical comparisons are part of the result

- Keep pooled and matched controls attached to the panels that display them.
- Preserve the recorded multiple-testing family; do not reinterpret a global
  q value as a per-timepoint test.
- For the **123-CpG reference**, the Figure 4o centre tests the average matched
  displacement over T1–T6, whereas the right panel tests the T5–T6 endpoint.
  Neither label is a test of an increasing temporal slope.
- hTERT final-cycle and whole-series tests are separate endpoints.
- CpGs and repeated timepoints do not increase the number of independent runs.

## Build the documentation locally

From the repository root:

```sh
python3 scripts/build_docs.py
python3 scripts/check_repository.py
quarto render docs
quarto preview docs --host 127.0.0.1
```

These commands build and serve local documentation only. They do not deploy
GitHub Pages, run analyses or download data. Python 3 uses only its standard
library for the documentation preparation script.

## Release status

The input package has been uploaded to an unpublished Zenodo draft; the website
remains a local preview. Before public release, we will reconcile the remaining
reconstruction labels, complete access and licensing checks, record software
environments and test chapter execution. See the
[release checklist](https://github.com/BolisLab/mir29/blob/main/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md).
